propositions.text: The Principal and Associate Appellants are Nepalese citizens appealing the RPD's rejection of their refugee claims.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX (the Principal Appellant) and his wife, XXXX XXXX (the Associate Appellant), are citizens of Nepal. They appeal a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rejecting their claims for refugee protection.

propositions.text: They fear persecution by Biplav Maoists due to the Principal Appellant's political opinion as an RPP member.
propositions.quote: The Appellants allege a fear of persecution from the Biplav (Biplab) Maoists upon return to Nepal based on the Principal Appellant's political opinion, as a member of the opposition Rastriya Prajatantra Party Nepal (RPP), also known as the National Democratic Party Nepal.

propositions.text: They argue the RPD erred in finding their claim not objectively well-founded.
propositions.quote: The Appellants argue that the RPD erred when it found their claim is not objectively well-founded.

propositions.text: After independent assessment, the RPD erred; the claim is well-founded and they are Convention refugees.
propositions.quote: Having independently assessed all of the evidence, including the RPD hearing audio-recording, I find that the RPD erred. I find that the Appellants' claim is well-founded and that they are Convention refugees.

propositions.text: I address why the RPD's findings are erroneous before giving reasons for allowing the appeal.
propositions.quote: I have addressed why the RPD's findings are in error before providing my reasons for allowing the appeal and accepting the Appellants' claims.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Nepalese appellants' refugee claim well-founded, rejects the RPD's contrary finding, and will explain why.

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed; the RAD sets aside the RPD's decision and substitutes its own that the Appellant is a Convention refugee.
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed. The Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) sets aside the determination of the RPD and substitutes its own determination that the Appellant is a Convention refugee.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD allows the appeal and replaces the RPD's decision with its own finding the appellant is a Convention refugee.

propositions.text: The Principal Appellant alleges Maoists seized family land in 2005 for non-cooperation.
propositions.quote: The Principal Appellant alleges that Maoists seized his family land in Sarlahi in 2005 as retribution for not cooperating with their cause.

propositions.text: He alleges multiple acts of political persecution during the civil war due to RPP activities.
propositions.quote: During the course of the civil war, the Principal Appellant alleges multiple acts of political persecution as a result of his RPP activities.

propositions.text: He lived many years in Qatar as a temporary resident.
propositions.quote: As a result, he has lived for many years in Qatar as a temporary resident.

propositions.text: After 2006 CPA, he asked local administration to return family property but Maoists refused.
propositions.quote: After the Comprehensive Peace Accord (CPA) was signed in 2006, the Principal Appellant alleges that he asked the local administration to facilitate the return of the family property. However, the Maoists refused.

propositions.text: He is responsible for ensuring family land is returned due to father's illness and brother's poor relationship.
propositions.quote: He alleges that due to his father's illness and his only brother's poor relationship with the family, he is in charge of ensuring the family land is returned.

paragraphs.summary: The Principal Appellant alleges Maoists seized family land, persecuted him politically, he lived in Qatar, and he seeks family land return.

propositions.text: In 2011, he was physically attacked by Maoists after inquiring about family land return.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2011, the Principal Appellant alleges that he was physically attacked by Maoists after he enquired about the return of his family's land.

propositions.text: In 2018, they decided to return permanently to Nepal after new constitution promulgation.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2018, the Appellants decided to return permanently to Nepal from Qatar following the promulgation of the new constitution.

propositions.text: Biplav Maoists took control of family property.
propositions.quote: He alleges that the Biplav faction of the Maoists gained control of his family property.

propositions.text: In 2018, he was attacked and threatened by Biplav Maoists for political opinion and land demand.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX, 2018, the Principal Appellant alleges that he was physically attacked and threatened by Biplav Maoists who told him that they are not just after him because of his demand for his family land but also because of his political opinion.

propositions.text: They threatened to kill him if he does not fund and join their party.
propositions.quote: They threatened to kill him if he does not fund and join their party.

propositions.text: He was threatened again in Kathmandu in 2018.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2018, the Principal Appellant was threatened again, this time in Kathmandu.

propositions.text: In 2018, both appellants were threatened and attacked, causing Associate Appellant's miscarriage.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX, 2018, the Appellants allege that they were threatened with death and physically attacked, resulting in the Associate Appellant's miscarriage.

propositions.text: They fled Nepal for Canada in 2018 and initiated refugee claims shortly after arrival.
propositions.quote: They fled Nepal for Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2018, initiating their refugee claims shortly after their arrival.

paragraphs.summary: The Principal Appellant alleges multiple attacks and threats by Biplav Maoists in 2018, leading to flight to Canada and refugee claims.

propositions.text: RPD noted inconsistency about reasons for visits to Nepal but made no adverse credibility findings.
propositions.quote: The RPD notes that an inconsistency arose in the Principal Appellant's testimony regarding the reason for his visits to Nepal in 2011 and 2014, whether to care for his ailing father or for his marriage. However, the RPD does not make any adverse credibility findings with respect to the Appellants' allegations.

propositions.text: RPD found claim not objectively well-founded; no serious persecution risk if land claim abandoned.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Appellants' claim is not objectively well-founded. Specifically, that the Appellants do not face a serious possibility of persecution upon return to Nepal if the Principal Appellant discontinues his quest to reclaim his family land.

propositions.text: RPD found Biplav Maoists pose generalized risk; Principal Appellant not prime target due to political profile.
propositions.quote: The RPD also found that the Biplav Maoists pose a "generalized risk" and that the Principal Appellant's political profile would not make him a prime target for the Biplav Maoists.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found no adverse credibility issues but rejected the claim as not well-founded, seeing only generalized risk from Maoists.

propositions.text: I conducted an independent assessment and review the RPD decision on correctness standard.
propositions.quote: I have conducted an independent assessment of the evidence. I am reviewing the RPD's decision on the correctness standard as I do not find the RPD enjoyed a meaningful advantage.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD independently assessed the evidence and reviews the RPD decision on a correctness standard.

propositions.text: No new evidence submitted; RAD has no jurisdiction to hold oral hearing.
propositions.quote: The Appellants have not submitted new evidence in support of their appeal. Having admitted no new evidence, the RAD has no jurisdiction to convene an oral hearing.

paragraphs.summary: No new evidence was submitted, so the RAD cannot hold an oral hearing.

propositions.text: Counsel argues RPD failed to assess totality of evidence before finding claim not well-founded.
propositions.quote: Counsel argues that this finding was made without assessing the totality of the evidence.

propositions.text: I agree RPD erred after independent assessment including hearing audio-recording.
propositions.quote: After listening to the RPD hearing audio-recording and independently assessing all of the evidence, I find that the RPD erred.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel argues RPD erred by not assessing all evidence; the court agrees after independent review.

propositions.text: RPD found persecution was punitive for land reclamation efforts; safe return if land claim abandoned.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the persecution arose as a punitive measure for the Principal Appellant's efforts to reclaim his family land. As a result, the RPD found that the Appellants could safely return to Nepal should the Principal Appellant discontinue his quest to reclaim his family land.

propositions.text: Claimants must pursue reasonable choices to avoid harm, including abandoning claims to property.
propositions.quote: Generally speaking, "[C]laimants who are able to make reasonable choices and thereby free themselves of a risk of harm must be expected to pursue those options."

propositions.text: It is not error to expect claimants to abandon property claims to avoid persecution.
propositions.quote: In this context, it is not an error for the RPD to expect a Claimant to abandon their claim to property in order to avoid persecution in their country of nationality.

propositions.text: This principle applies only if claimant is not required to compromise identity or fundamental belief.
propositions.quote: However, this principle only applies where a Claimant is not being required to compromise either who they are or a fundamental belief.

propositions.text: I find RPD erred applying this principle in this claim.
propositions.quote: For the following reasons, I find that the RPD erred in applying this principle in the Appellants' claim.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD erred applying the law that claimants must abandon property claims to avoid harm when identity or beliefs are compromised.

propositions.text: Principal Appellant alleges Biplav Maoists target him for political opinion as RPP member supporting monarchy.
propositions.quote: The Principal Appellant alleges that the Biplav Maoists explicitly told him that they continue to target him because he is a member of the RPP who supports the monarchy and hates the Maoists, peasants, and the poor.

propositions.text: RPD does not impugn credibility of this allegation.
propositions.quote: The RPD does not impugn the credibility of this allegation.

propositions.text: Persecutors target him not only for land claim but also political opinion; abandoning land claim may not avoid persecution.
propositions.quote: It is not the case that the agents of persecution are only interested in the Principal Appellant because of his attempts to reclaim his family land. As such, it is not clear that abandoning the property claim would enable the Appellants to return to Nepal without facing a serious possibility of persecution.

propositions.text: RPD's finding on this point is in error.
propositions.quote: The RPD's finding is in error.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred in ignoring that persecution is also for political opinion, not just land claim.

propositions.text: RPD found Principal Appellant's political profile would not make him a prime target for Biplav Maoists.
propositions.quote: The RPD also found that the Principal Appellant's profile would not entice his agents of persecution to force him to join their organization and notes that his political profile would not make him a prime target for the Biplav Maoists.

propositions.text: RPD gave no objective evidence for this finding; unclear basis for it.
propositions.quote: The RPD does not refer to any objective evidence in support of this finding. It is unclear upon what basis the RPD found that the Principal Appellant's political opinion and profile would not place him and the Associate Appellant at a serious possibility of persecution upon return to Nepal.

propositions.text: Appellants survived three politically motivated attacks including violence, threats, and demands before fleeing Nepal.
propositions.quote: It is especially unclear when considered in light of the Appellants' uncontradicted allegation that they have survived no less than three politically motivated attacks from the Biplav Maoists - including physical violence, death threats, and demands for money and party membership - prior to fleeing Nepal.

propositions.text: Personal documentary evidence corroborates political affiliation, land ownership, reports, and attacks.
propositions.quote: The Appellants' personal documentary evidence corroborates the Principal Appellant's political affiliation, land ownership, multiple reports to authorities, and physical attacks.

propositions.text: RPD's finding on political profile and persecution risk is in error.
propositions.quote: The RPD's finding is in error.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred in finding no serious persecution risk from political profile, lacking objective evidence and ignoring attacks.

propositions.text: RPD found a generalized risk from Biplav Maoists.
propositions.quote: Finally, the RPD's finding of "generalized risk" is misplaced.

propositions.text: Principal Appellant alleged nexus to Convention ground based on political opinion; RPD did not find lack of nexus.
propositions.quote: The Principal Appellant alleged a nexus to a Convention ground based on his political opinion. The RPD did not make a finding that the Appellants lack a nexus to a Convention ground.

propositions.text: Generalized risk analysis applies to subsection 97(1) claims, not to serious possibility of persecution under section 96.
propositions.quote: A generalized risk analysis is applicable to claims assessed under subsection 97(1) and not to claims alleging a serious possibility of persecution under section 96 of the IRPA.

propositions.text: I find the RPD erred in applying generalized risk analysis here.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD erred.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred by applying generalized risk analysis instead of assessing nexus to persecution ground.

propositions.text: After own assessment, Appellants face serious possibility of persecution and claims are well-founded.
propositions.quote: Having conducted my own assessment of the evidence, I find that the Appellants face a serious possibility of persecution upon return to Nepal and that their claims are well-founded.

propositions.text: NDP shows Maoist factions retained illegally seized land and many land disputes remain.
propositions.quote: The National Documentation Package (NDP) for Nepal indicates that following the CPA, Maoist factions have retained illegally seized land and a "a significant number of conflict-era land disputes remained outstanding."

propositions.text: NDP shows Biplav Maoists involved in kidnapping, violence, and extortion.
propositions.quote: The NDP also indicates that the Biplav (Biplab) Maoist faction is involved in kidnapping, physical violence, and extortion.

propositions.text: Maoist attacks on opposition reduced but continuing attacks reported.
propositions.quote: While information in the NDP indicates that Maoist attacks on opposition members have reduced, there are reports of continuing attacks.

propositions.text: April 2019 Al Jazeera article says Biplav faction is growing in strength and fueled by disillusionment.
propositions.quote: Counsel's April 2019 article from Al Jazeera indicates that the Biplav faction is "fed by popular disillusionment and anger" and that it is "growing in strength."

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellants face serious persecution risk supported by NDP and media reports of Maoist violence and growing Biplav faction.

propositions.text: Claimants must show more than mere possibility of persecution; this is a low threshold.
propositions.quote: The Appellants must only make out more than a mere possibility of persecution in order to succeed in their claim for refugee protection. This is a low threshold.

propositions.text: I find the possibility of persecution by reason of political opinion is more than mere possibility.
propositions.quote: I find that the possibility that the Appellants will face persecution - including serious physical violence - by reason of the Principal Appellant's political opinion to be more than a mere one.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellants meet the low threshold of more than mere possibility of persecution due to political opinion.

propositions.text: Whether appellants have access to adequate state protection or viable internal flight alternative.
propositions.quote: Having found that the Appellants face more than a mere possibility of persecution, I have also considered whether the Appellants have access to operationally adequate state protection in Nepal or a viable Internal Flight Alternative (IFA).

paragraphs.summary: The court considers if appellants have state protection or internal flight alternative in Nepal.

propositions.text: Nepal government banned Biplav faction as criminal group in March 2019.
propositions.quote: In March 2019 the Nepalese government officially declared the Biplav (Biplap) faction a criminal group and banned all of its activities.

propositions.text: Many local Maoist leaders sympathize with Biplav faction; ban increased faction's popularity and tensions.
propositions.quote: "many local Maoist leaders have at least some sympathy for Biplab's party" and the ban has served to bolster the faction's popularity and increase tensions.

propositions.text: NDP indicates police are not independent and fail to investigate promptly and impartially.
propositions.quote: The NDP indicates that the police are not independent and often fail to carry out prompt, thorough, and impartial investigations.

propositions.text: Appellants sought protection multiple times but received no assistance.
propositions.quote: Despite seeking protection on multiple occasions, the Appellants were not provided with assistance.

propositions.text: Nepal has weakened criminal justice system and impunity.
propositions.quote: Nepal continues to suffer from a weakened criminal justice system and impunity.

propositions.text: On balance of probabilities, appellants lack access to adequate state protection in Nepal.
propositions.quote: I find, on a balance of probabilities, that the Appellants do not have access to adequate state protection in Nepal.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Nepal's ban on Biplav faction ineffective; police are not independent; appellants lack adequate state protection.

propositions.text: Nepal is small; Biplav Maoists have nationwide network.
propositions.quote: The NPD indicates that Nepal is a small country and that the Biplav Maoists have a nation-wide network.

propositions.text: Appellants were located by persecutors in multiple cities; no viable internal flight alternative exists.
propositions.quote: The Appellants were located by their agents of persecution in multiple cities within Nepal. On this basis, I find that the Appellants face a serious possibility of persecution throughout Nepal and that they do not have a viable IFA.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellants face persecution throughout Nepal and have no viable internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: Appeal allowed; RAD sets aside RPD decision and finds appellants are Convention refugees.
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed. Pursuant to section 111(1)(b) of the IRPA, the RAD sets aside the determination of the RPD and substitutes its own determination that the Appellants are Convention refugees.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD allows the appeal and finds the appellants are Convention refugees, setting aside the RPD decision.
